newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-NUGGETS BEAT NETS 132-123 IN SEASON'S HIGHEST-SCORING GAME.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-NUGGETS BEAT NETS 132-123 IN SEASON'S HIGHEST-SCORING GAME.

text.p: LaPhonso Ellis scored a career-high 36 points and Antonio McDyess returned to the lineup with 29 as the Denver Nuggets defeated the New Jersey Nets, 132-123 on Monday.
It was the highest scoring game this season, eclipsing the Chicago Bulls 129-123 overtime win against the Los Angeles Lakers.
Mark Jackson had 21 points and 22 assists for the Nuggets.

"Hats off to our guys, we stayed cool and didn't blow our lead," Ellis said. "A couple of weeks ago who knows it all starts with Jackson, he's so savvy and keen to get us the ball at the right times."

In Atlanta, Steve Smith scored a season-high 31 points and Christian Laettner added 23 as the Atlanta Hawks built an 18-point fourth-quarter lead and held off the Charlotte Hornets, 106-97 for their 10th straight win.
Mookie Blaylock contributed 20 points and 10 assists for the Hawks. Glen Rice scored 33 points and Vlade Divac had 21 for the Hornets, who had their four-game winning streak snapped.
In Los Angeles, Nick Van Exel had 24 points as the Los Angeles Lakers snapped a two-game home losing streak with a 109-99 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.
Eddie Jones added 21 points and Elden Campbell 17 for the Lakers, who beat the Mavericks for the 19th time in the last 21 games.
Jim Jackson had 22 points and Chris Gatling 21 for Dallas.
Shaquille O'Neal, who saw his streak of 28 straight games with 20 or more points end Saturday, finished with 14 points and 13 rebounds for the Lakers.

At Minnesota, rookie Stephon Marbury scored 20 points and had a career-high 13 assists and Kevin Garnett also scored 20 points as the Minnesota Timberwolves cruised to a 96-83 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.
Tom Gugliotta had 18 points and 12 rebounds for Minnesota.
"We are starting to jell together as a team," said Minneosta guard James Robinson, who had 17 points, five rebounds and four assists. "The biggest thing is we are trusting each other on defence."
In New York, Buck Williams scored 13 of his season-high 17 points in the first half as the New York Knicks continued their mastery of the Washington Bullets with a 95-79 victory.
Patrick Ewing had 22 points and 14 rebounds for New York.
"I thought we had great energy," said New York coach Jeff Van Gundy. "We have to learn how to play from behind and with the lead."
Chris Webber scored 17 points and Juwan Howard 13 for Washington.
In Phoenix, Kevin Johnson scored 19 points and had a key steal with four seconds remaining as the Phoenix Suns rallied for an 89-86 victory over the Detroit Pistons.
Cedric Ceballos had 18 points and Rex Chapman 17 for the Suns, who scored a season-low 33 points in the first half and erased a 15-point third-quarter deficit.

"That was the best game of the year," Phoenix coach Danny Ainge said. "Our starters were a little sluggish the first half and when they (Detroit) started hitting the threes, their (the Suns) heads were dropping."
In Seattle, Gary Payton scored 30 points and Shawn Kemp added 23 as the Seattle SuperSonics remained perfect in 1997, knocking off the Vancouver Grizzlies, 112-96.
Detlef Schrempf chipped in 20 points, seven rebounds, seven assists and three steals for Seattle, which is 8-0 in the new year and has won 12 of 14 games.
Jim McIlvaine had 10 points for the Sonics.
